question.text: Ms. Priya Shah (IM of Kalinga PE Fund, Cat II) is debating with LPs whether to pay carry on a DEAL-BY-DEAL basis or only at END OF FUND TENURE. Which statement is accurate per Chapter 6 treatment of these two mechanisms?

answer.text: End-of-fund carry eliminates the need for clawback; deal-by-deal carry often requires robust clawback + escrow arrangements
Deal-by-deal carry eliminates double-counting of gains; end-of-fund carry compounds the IM's take
Both mechanisms are mathematically identical; only the timing of tax differs
Deal-by-deal carry is prohibited for Category II AIFs under SEBI regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: End-of-fund carry is 'self-correcting' — by the time it's computed, all losses are netted. Deal-by-deal carry creates the risk that EARLY winners trigger carry that LATER losses reverse — hence CLAWBACK + GP-level escrow is essential. Chapter 6 explicitly links clawback to deal-by-deal distribution. The Trap: B is inverted; C ignores the clawback risk; D is false — deal-by-deal is permitted for Cat I/II. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this. XIX-E (Cat III) uses daily/periodic HWM-based crystallisation — a different animal, not deal-by-deal. Manager's Pro-Tip: If you adopt deal-by-deal carry to compete on LP terms, add: (i) minimum 25-30% GP-level escrow on carry until final exit; (ii) annual clawback true-up; (iii) GP personal guarantees if GP entity is thinly capitalised. LPs will thank you.
